SELECTED_INDEX: 5
CONFIDENCE: 0.22
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by bands typical of an aromatic system with one or two hetero-atom substituents.  

• Strong C–H stretching at 3082 cm⁻¹ together with intense ring ν(C=C) bands at 1609 and 1572 cm⁻¹ indicate an sp²-rich (benzene-like) framework.  
• Two very strong C–H out-of-plane deformation bands at 847 and 830 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of a 1,2,4-substituted benzene ring, matching the substitution pattern of O=c1cc(Br)cco1.  
• The 632 cm⁻¹ band fits the typical ν(C–Br) stretch of aryl bromides (600–650 cm⁻¹), supporting the presence of a bromine substituent found only in candidate 5.  
• Bands at 1157 and 1235 cm⁻¹ correspond to C–O (aryl–O) and C–O–C stretches of an aromatic ring incorporating an oxygen, again consistent with the benzofuran-one skeleton of candidate 5.  
• Additional medium bands at 1428 and 1403 cm⁻¹ are normal aromatic C–C/C–H deformations.

No other candidate combines an aromatic ring, an internal hetero-oxygen (C–O–C), a conjugated carbonyl, and an aromatic C–Br bond required to explain the key 632 cm⁻¹ peak. Therefore candidate 5 best fits the observed Raman features.
